q: 101. The ratio of minimum number of longitudinal bars provided in rectangular columns to those in circular column is ...........
explain: Rectangular columns require a minimum of 4 bars (one in each corner), while circular columns require a minimum of 6 bars. The ratio is 4/6, which simplifies to 2/3.

q: 102. Spacing of longitudinal bars measured along the peripheral of the column should not exceed ...........
explain: As per IS 456, the maximum spacing between longitudinal bars along the periphery of the column is limited to 300 mm to prevent local buckling of the concrete face.

q: 103. The nominal longitudinal reinforcement in pedestals should not be less than ...........
explain: For pedestals (where length is less than 3 times the least lateral dimension), the minimum longitudinal reinforcement is 0.15% of the gross cross-sectional area.

q: 104. A pedestal is said to be a compression member when its effective length does not exceed ...........
options: two times the least lateral dimension
three times the least lateral dimension
four times the least lateral dimension
explain: A vertical compression member is classified as a pedestal if its effective length is less than or equal to 3 times its least lateral dimension.

q: 105. The internal angle of laterals ties in the form of polygonal links in columns shall not exceed ...........
explain: To ensure effective lateral restraint and prevent the tie from 'opening' under pressure, the internal angle of a polygonal link should not exceed 135°.

q: 106. The diameter of the helical reinforcement should not be less than X-times the diameter of the largest longitudinal bar subject to a minimum of 5 mm, where X is ...........
explain: The diameter of transverse or helical reinforcement must be at least one-fourth (1/4) the diameter of the largest longitudinal bar, with a minimum of 5 mm (or 6mm in modern practice).

q: 107. All compression members are designed for minimum eccentricity equal to ...........
options: unsupported length of column/500 plus lateral dimension/30 subject to a minimum of 20 mm
unsupported length of column/400 plus lateral dimension/30 subject to a minimum of 20 mm
supported length of column/500 plus lateral dimension/30 subject to a minimum of 20 mm
unsupported length of column/400 plus lateral dimension/30 subject to a minimum of 20 mm
explain: IS 456 defines minimum eccentricity as (L/500) + (D/30), where L is unsupported length and D is lateral dimension, but it cannot be less than 20 mm.

q: 108. The minimum number of longitudinal steel bars in R.C.C. rectangular columns must be ...........
explain: Every corner of a rectangular or square column must have a bar to provide symmetrical reinforcement and tie the cage, necessitating at least 4 bars.

q: 109. The minimum number of longitudinal steel bars in R.C.C. circular columns must be ...........
explain: For circular columns, 6 bars are required to properly maintain the circular shape of the reinforcement cage and provide uniform confinement.

q: 110. The minimum number of longitudinal steel bars in helically reinforced R.C.C. columns must be ...........
explain: Helical reinforcement is typically used in circular columns, which requires a minimum of 6 longitudinal bars for stability of the helix.

q: 111. Spacing of longitudinal bars measured along the periphery of a circular R.C.C. column shall not exceed ...........
explain: The 300 mm maximum spacing rule applies to all column shapes, including circular ones, to ensure the concrete surface is effectively reinforced.

q: 112. The maximum spacing of longitudinal bars with a tie bent around alternate bars in R.C.C columns is ...........
explain: If bars are not effectively tied (i.e., the tie only wraps alternate bars), the maximum distance between a tied bar and an untied bar is 150 mm.

q: 113. The spacing of the longitudinal bars effectively tied should not exceed the following if additional longitudinal bars provided in between are tied in one direction by open ties ...........
explain: Specific detailing requirements for secondary ties/links often relate spacing to the diameter of the transverse reinforcement (48 times the tie diameter).

q: 114. The diameter of transverse reinforcement of columns should be equal to one fourth of the diameter of the main rods but not less than ...........
explain: While 5mm was the older standard, current practice (and many code versions) specifies a 6 mm minimum for transverse ties to ensure cage rigidity.

q: 115. The spacing of transverse reinforcement of a column shall not be more than ...........
options: the least lateral dimension of a column
sixteen times the smallest diameter of the longitudinal reinforcement bar to be tied
forty-eight times the diameter of the transverse reinforcement
explain: IS 456 pitch requirements for ties: Spacing should be the least of: 1) Least lateral dimension, 2) 16x smallest longitudinal bar diameter, or 3) 48x tie diameter.

q: 116. If the size of a column is reduced above the floor, the main bars of the column are ...........
options: bent inward at the floor level
stopped just below the floor level and separate bars are provided
explain: Bars can be cranked (bent) inward if the offset is small (slope 1 in 6); otherwise, they are terminated and new starter bars are lapped.

q: 117. Generally for piles, the concrete used is of grade ...........
explain: M20 is generally the minimum grade for reinforced concrete in foundations (like piles) to ensure durability against groundwater and soil chemicals.

q: 118. Concrete fails at a strain of ...........
explain: In the Limit State of collapse (flexure), the maximum strain in concrete at the outermost compression fiber is assumed to be 0.0035.

q: 119. The shape of the stress-strain curve of concrete up to a strain of 0.002 is ...........
explain: The idealized stress-strain curve for concrete consists of a parabolic portion from zero strain to 0.002, followed by a rectangular portion up to 0.0035.

q: 120. The shape stress-strain curve of mild steel up to yield stress is ...........
explain: Mild steel is a linearly elastic material up to its yield point, meaning stress is directly proportional to strain.

q: 121. In the case of Fe 415 and Fe 500 steels, the yield stress is taken as ....... percent proof stress.
explain: High-strength steels do not have a well-defined yield point, so the yield stress is taken as the stress corresponding to a 0.2% permanent (offset) strain.

q: 122. The moment of resistance factor Ru is given as ...........
explain: The Moment of Resistance (Mu) is calculated as $M_u = R_u \cdot b \cdot d^2$, making $R_u = M_u / (b \cdot d^2)$.

q: 123. Over reinforced section is not desirable because ...........
options: failure is sudden as concrete fails first
explain: In over-reinforced sections, concrete reaches its failure strain before the steel yields, leading to a brittle, explosive failure without warning.

q: 124. The balanced design gives ...........
explain: A balanced section utilizes the full capacity of both materials simultaneously, resulting in the most compact concrete section for a given set of materials.

q: 125. In a simply supported beam carrying uniformly distributed load, the spacing of vertical stumps near supports would be ...........
explain: Shear force is maximum at the supports. To resist this higher shear, stirrups (vertical reinforcement) must be spaced closer together.

q: 126. For a fixed beam of span l carrying uniformly distributed load the bending moment at the critical section is given by ...........
explain: For a fixed-ended beam with UDL, the maximum bending moment occurs at the supports (fixed ends) and is equal to $wl^2/12$.

q: 127. In general the formula for short terms deflection at the mid span can be expressed as ...........
explain: Standard deflection formulas for beams under distributed loads are proportional to $W \cdot L^4$ (or $P \cdot L^3$ for point loads).

q: 128. As per I.S. 456: 2000, the vertical deflection limits in a cantilever beam may generally be assumed to be satisfied provided that (span/depth) ratio does not exceed ...........
explain: To control deflection, IS 456 specifies basic span-to-effective-depth ratios: 7 for cantilevers, 20 for simply supported, and 26 for continuous beams.

q: 129. The moment of resistance factor Ru, lim when Fe415 steel is used, is given by ...........
explain: For Fe415 steel, the limiting moment of resistance factor is $0.138 \cdot f_{ck}$ based on the strain limit in steel.

q: 130. Which of the following is not a measure adopted for reducing deflection?
explain: Decreasing reinforcement would actually increase deflection; to reduce it, one should increase stiffness (depth or concrete grade) or use camber.

q: 131. The assessed surface width of crack should not generally exceed ...........
explain: While 0.3mm is allowed for mild exposure, many design specifications (especially in older or more stringent codes) target 0.2mm for better durability.

q: 132. Working stress design assumes ...........
explain: The Working Stress Method is based on the elastic theory, assuming that both steel and concrete behave linearly and elastically under service loads.

q: 133. Working stress design assumes ...........
options: partial recovery of deflections caused during some load condition
full recovery of deflections caused during some load conditions
partial recovery of deflections caused in all types of load conditions
full recovery of deflections caused in all types of load conditions
explain: Because it assumes perfect elasticity, the WSM implies that when the load is removed, the structure returns to its original shape (full recovery).

q: 134. The stresses caused by different loads can be superimposed in ...........
explain: Superposition is only valid in linear-elastic systems. Working Stress Method is the only one listed that assumes linear elasticity.

q: 135. The approximate allowable stress in bending compression in reinforced concrete is ...........
explain: In WSM, the permissible stress in bending compression (sigma_cbc) is roughly $f_{ck}/3$, which is approximately $0.33 \cdot f_{ck}$.

q: 136. The approximate allowable stress in axial compression in reinforced concrete is ...........
explain: In WSM, the permissible stress in direct (axial) compression (sigma_cc) is roughly $f_{ck}/4$, which is $0.25 \cdot f_{ck}$.

q: 137. The design shear stress in reinforced cement concrete depends on ...........
explain: Design shear strength (tau_c) is a function of the concrete grade and the amount of tension steel (which restricts crack opening).

q: 138. The maximum shear stress permitted in reinforced concrete members depends upon ...........
explain: The absolute maximum shear stress (tau_c max) is limited solely based on the grade of concrete to prevent diagonal compression failure of the web.

q: 139. The ratio of the allowable bond stress in deformed bars to that of plain bars is about ...........
explain: IS 456 allows for a 60% increase (ratio of 1.6) in bond stress for deformed (HYSD) bars compared to plain mild steel bars.

q: 140. The ultimate tensile stress in mild steel bars of grade I should be greater than (in N/mm2) ...........
explain: Grade I mild steel typically has an ultimate tensile strength exceeding 415 N/mm², even if its yield stress is lower (around 250 N/mm²).

q: 141. The allowable tensile stress in mild steel stirrups in reinforced cement concrete is (in N/mm2) ...........
explain: For mild steel (Fe 250) used as shear reinforcement in WSM, the permissible tensile stress is 140 N/mm².

q: 142. In the limit state method the over-reinforced sections ...........
options: are permitted only in extreme cases
explain: Limit State Design strictly prohibits over-reinforced sections to ensure that failure is always ductile (steel yields before concrete crushes).

q: 143. If the factored moment to be carried by a rectangular section is more than the limiting moment of the section ...........
options: the section can be designed as a over-reinforced section
the section has to be redesigned increasing the dimensions or design the section as doubly reinforced
explain: Since over-reinforcement is forbidden, you must either increase the beam size or add compression steel (doubly reinforced) to carry the extra moment.

q: 144. The allowable bond stress in tension for plain bars in the limit sate method for M15 grade concrete is ...........
explain: For M15 concrete in Limit State Method, the design bond stress (tau_bd) for plain bars is 1.0 N/mm².

q: 145. In the limit state method, the maximum compressive strain in axial compression in concrete is taken as ...........
explain: While 0.0035 is for flexure, in cases of pure axial compression, the failure strain across the entire section is taken as 0.002.

q: 146. In a singly reinforced beam, the effective depth is measured from its compression edge to ...........
explain: Effective depth 'd' is the distance from the extreme compression fiber to the center of gravity of the tensile reinforcement.

q: 147. If the modular ratio is m, steel ratio is r = sigma_st / nbc and overall depth of a beam is d, the depth of the critical neutral axis of the beam is ...........
explain: Derived from the properties of similar triangles in the stress diagram of a balanced section: $x_c = [m \cdot \sigma_{cbc} / (m \cdot \sigma_{cbc} + \sigma_{st})] \cdot d$.

q: 148. If d and n are the effective depth and depth of the neutral axis respectively of a singly reinforced beam, the lever arm of the beam is ...........
explain: Lever arm is the distance between the total compressive force (acting at n/3 from the top) and the tensile force: $z = d - n/3$.

q: 149. The section of a reinforced beam where most distant concrete fibre in compression and tension in steel attains permissible stresses simultaneously, is called ...........
explain: A balanced section is also known as a critical section (where neutral axis is at critical depth) and is often the most economical in terms of material usage.

q: 150. In a singly reinforced beam, if the permissible stress in concrete reaches earlier than that in steel, the beam section is called ...........
explain: If concrete reaches its limit first, it means there is 'too much' steel for the concrete to handle, hence 'over-reinforced'.

q: 151. As the percentage of steel increases ............
explain: In a reinforced concrete beam, the depth of the neutral axis is directly proportional to the reinforcement ratio. Increasing the steel area requires a larger concrete compression area to maintain equilibrium, thus pushing the neutral axis deeper.

q: 152. By over-reinforcing a beam, the moment resistance can be increased not more than ............
explain: According to limit state design principles, over-reinforcing a section beyond the balanced condition provides diminishing returns in moment capacity, generally capped around 25% due to the brittle nature of concrete failure.

q: 153. Distribution of shear intensity over a rectangular section of a beam, follows ............
explain: For a homogenous rectangular section, the shear stress distribution is parabolic, with the maximum stress occurring at the neutral axis and zero at the top and bottom fibers.

q: 154. According to I.S.: 456 specifications, the safe diagonal tensile stress for M150 grade concrete is ............
explain: Under older metric codes (like M150/M15), the permissible shear stress (which represents diagonal tension) for lower grades of concrete is approximately 5 kg/cm².

q: 155. Dimension of a beam need be changed if the shear stress is more than ............
explain: If the nominal shear stress exceeds the maximum permissible shear stress ($	au_{c,max}$), which is around 20 kg/cm² for M15/M150, the section is unsafe against diagonal compression and dimensions must be increased.

q: 156. The maximum shear stress (q) in concrete of a reinforced cement concrete beam is ............
explain: In the working stress method, the nominal shear stress $q$ is calculated as $V / (b \cdot z)$, where $V$ is shear force, $b$ is width, and $z$ is the lever arm.

q: 157. If $S_b$ is the average bond stress on a bar of diameter $d$ subjected to maximum stress $t$, the length of the embedment $l$ is given by ............
explain: The development length is derived by equating the force in the bar to the bond force: $(\pi d^2 / 4) \cdot t = \pi d \cdot l \cdot S_b$. Solving for $l$ gives $dt / 4S_b$.

q: 158. If the average bending stress is 6 kg/cm² for M150 grade concrete, the length of embedment of a bar of diameter $d$ according to I.S. 456 specifications, is ............
explain: For M150 concrete and mild steel in tension, the development length requirement typically works out to approximately 58 times the diameter of the bar ($58d$).

q: 159. In a beam the local bond stress $S_b$ is equal to ............
options: shear force / (lever arm × total perimeter of reinforcement)
explain: Local (flexural) bond stress is calculated as $V / (\sum O \cdot j \cdot d)$, where $\sum O$ is the total perimeter of the reinforcement.

q: 160. For M150 mix concrete, according to I.S. specifications, local bond stress, is ............
explain: For an M150 (M15 equivalent) mix, the permissible local bond stress is specifically defined as 10 kg/cm² in the standard tables.

q: 161. If diameter of a reinforcement bar is d, the anchorage value of the hook is ............
explain: A standard U-type hook (180 degree bend) provides an anchorage value equivalent to 16 times the diameter of the bar ($16d$).

q: 162. The radius of a bar bend to form a hook, should not be less than ............
explain: To prevent internal stress concentration and cracking of the steel, the minimum radius for a bend in mild steel is 2 times the bar diameter.

q: 163. The length of the straight portion of a bar beyond the end of the hook, should be at least ............
explain: IS 456 specifies that the straight length of the bar beyond the end of the curve shall be at least 4 times the diameter of the bar.

q: 164. Minimum spacing between horizontal parallel reinforcement of the same size should be less than ............
explain: To ensure proper concrete flow and bonding, the horizontal spacing between parallel bars should be at least equal to the diameter of the bar (or the maximum size of coarse aggregate plus 5mm).

q: 165. Minimum spacing between horizontal parallel reinforcement of different size should not be less than ............
options: twice the diameter of thinner bar
explain: When bars of different diameters are used, the horizontal spacing must not be less than the diameter of the larger/thicker bar.

q: 166. The minimum thickness of the cover at the end of a reinforcing bar should not be less than twice the diameter of the bar subject to a minimum of ............
explain: For end cover of reinforcing bars, the rule is $2 \phi$ or 15 mm, whichever is greater, to protect the bar ends from corrosion.

q: 167. The compression force $C_u$ resisted by the concrete above neutral axis will be acting at a distance ............ from the extreme compression fibre.
explain: In the Limit State Method parabolic stress block, the centroid of the compressive force is located at $0.416 x_u$ (approximately $3/7 x_u$) from the extreme compression fiber.

q: 168. To determine the modulus of rupture, the size of test specimen used is ............
explain: The standard beam specimen for the flexural strength (modulus of rupture) test is $150 	imes 150 	imes 700$ mm.

q: 169. In singly reinforced beams, steel reinforcement is provided in ............
explain: A singly reinforced beam is designed such that the steel is only placed in the tension zone to resist tensile stresses which concrete cannot.

q: 170. In a simply supported reinforced concrete beam, the reinforcement is placed ............
explain: In a simply supported beam, sagging occurs, meaning the bottom fibers are in tension. Therefore, reinforcement is placed below the neutral axis.

q: 171. In a singly reinforced beam, the effective depth is measured from the compression edge to the ............
explain: Effective depth ($d$) is the distance from the extreme compression fiber to the centroid (center) of the tensile reinforcement.

q: 172. In a singly reinforced concrete beam, if the load is very small ............
options: only steel bars will resist tension
both concrete and steel will resist tension
both concrete and steel will resist compression
explain: At very low loads (uncracked stage), the concrete remains intact and both the concrete and steel contribute to resisting tensile stresses.

q: 173. In a singly reinforced concrete beam, as the load increases ............
options: only steel bars will resist tension
both concrete and steel will resist tension
both concrete and steel will resist compression
explain: Once the tensile stress exceeds the modulus of rupture of concrete, the concrete cracks. Beyond this point, only the steel bars are assumed to resist the total tensile force.

q: 174. Normally, the tensile strength of concrete is about ............ of its compressive strength.
explain: Concrete is very weak in tension; its tensile strength is usually estimated at about 1/10th or 10-15% of its compressive strength.

q: 175. A reinforced concrete beam will crack if tensile stress set up in the concrete below the neutral axis is ............
explain: Cracking occurs as soon as the actual tensile stress in the concrete fibers exceeds its allowable tensile capacity (modulus of rupture).

q: 176. In a beam section, if the steel reinforcement is of such a magnitude that the permissible stresses in concrete and steel are developed simultaneously, the section is known as ............
explain: A section where both materials reach their maximum allowable stresses at the same time is variously referred to as a balanced, critical, or economical section.

q: 177. The section in which concrete is not fully stressed to its permissible value when stress in steel reaches its maximum value, is called ............
explain: In an under-reinforced section, the steel reaches its yield point first while the concrete stress remains below its ultimate capacity.

q: 178. The neutral axis of a balanced section is called ............
explain: The depth of the neutral axis corresponding to the balanced strain/stress condition is termed the Critical Neutral Axis.

q: 179. The moment of resistance of an under-reinforced section is computed on the basis of ............
explain: Since steel reaches its permissible limit first in an under-reinforced section, the moment of resistance is governed by the steel capacity ($M = A_st \cdot \sigma_{st} \cdot j \cdot d$).

q: 180. In an over-reinforced section ............
options: steel reinforcement is not fully stressed
explain: In an over-reinforced section, concrete reaches its maximum permissible stress before the steel, meaning the steel remains under-stressed.

q: 181. For an over reinforced (singly reinforced) rectangular reinforced concrete section ............
options: lever arm is less than balanced section
max steel stress = allowable steel stress
max concrete stress = allowable concrete stress
explain: By definition, an over-reinforced section fails by crushing of concrete, meaning the concrete reaches its allowable stress while the steel does not.

q: 182. The moment of resistance of an over-reinforced section is determined on the basis of ............
explain: In over-reinforced sections, the concrete is the limiting factor, so the moment of resistance is calculated based on the compressive capacity of the concrete.

q: 183. The neutral axis of an over-reinforced section falls ............
explain: Because there is more steel than required for a balanced section, the neutral axis must shift downward (below the critical N.A.) to provide a larger compression area to balance the tension.

q: 184. The deep beams are designed for ............
explain: According to traditional design rules, deep beams (where span-to-depth ratio is very low) are primarily designed for bending moment, though shear is also a critical check.

q: 185. The maximum permissible shear stress given in I.S. 456 : 1978 is based on ............
explain: The limit for $	au_{c,max}$ is set to prevent the concrete in the web from crushing due to diagonal compression before the shear reinforcement yields.

q: 186. When the lever arm of a reinforced concrete beam is z and width of beam is b, then the maximum shear stress in a beam subjected to shear force F will be equal to ............
explain: Maximum shear stress in Working Stress Method is calculated as Shear Force / (Width x Lever Arm).

q: 187. In a reinforced concrete beam, the shear stress distribution above the neutral axis follows a ............
explain: In the concrete above the neutral axis, the shear stress distribution follows a parabolic curve, similar to a standard homogenous rectangular section.

q: 188. Which one of the following sections... can resist the torsional moment of R.C.C beam section more efficiently...?
explain: Closed sections (like box sections) are significantly more efficient in resisting torsion compared to open sections because they provide a continuous path for the shear flow.

q: 189. For a reinforced concrete beam section, the shape of the shear stress diagram is ............
options: parabolic above N.A. and rectangular below N.A.
explain: In R.C. beams, shear stress is parabolic from the top fiber to the Neutral Axis, and then remains constant (rectangular) from the N.A. down to the center of steel.

q: 190. The chances of diagonal tension cracks in R.C.C. member reduce when ............
explain: Axial compression reduces the principal tensile stress, thereby delaying or preventing the formation of diagonal tension cracks.

q: 191. Shear reinforcement is provided in the form of ............
explain: Shear can be resisted using vertical stirrups, bent-up longitudinal bars (inclined bars), or a combination of both.

q: 192. For M15 grade concrete, shear reinforcement is necessary, if shear stress is more than ............
explain: If the calculated nominal shear stress $	au_v$ exceeds the permissible shear stress $	au_c$ of concrete (which for M15 is roughly 0.5 N/mm² depending on % steel), shear reinforcement must be provided.

q: 193. For M15 grade concrete, the section is to be redesigned if shear stress is more than ............
explain: Redesign is required if $	au_v$ exceeds $	au_{c,max}$. For M15 concrete, the maximum limit $	au_{c,max}$ is 2.5 N/mm² (LSM) or approximately 2.0 N/mm² in older contexts.

q: 194. The centre to centre spacing of vertical stirrups, in a rectangular beam, is ............
explain: Shear force is maximum at the supports and minimum at the center. Therefore, stirrups are placed closer together at the ends and the spacing is increased toward the center.

q: 195. The spacing of vertical stirrups in a rectangular beam is ............
explain: Since shear force is highest at supports, stirrups are needed most there, resulting in the minimum (closest) spacing.

q: 196. The number of stirrups resisting shear force, in a reinforced beam, is given by ............
explain: The number of stirrups crossing a diagonal crack (roughly at 45 degrees) is determined by the horizontal length of the crack (approx. equal to the lever arm $d$ or $z$) divided by the spacing $s$.

q: 197. A stirrups consists of ............ diameter mild steel bars round the tensile reinforcement.
explain: Stirrups are usually made from smaller diameter bars, typically ranging from 5mm to 12mm.

q: 198. When the steel bars are embedded in concrete... The intensity of this adhesive force is called ............
explain: Bond stress is the longitudinal shear stress acting on the surface between the steel and the surrounding concrete which prevents relative movement.

q: 199. The longitudinal shearing stress acting on the surface between the steel and concrete are called ............
explain: As per the definition, this longitudinal shear interaction is called Bond Stress.

q: 200. The bond between steel and concrete is mainly due to ............
explain: Bonding is a combination of chemical adhesion, friction between the surfaces, and mechanical interlocking (especially in deformed bars).
